compute.device: BlueGene/P and PKS-AIMS (MPG RZG), SHARCNET; distributed-memory CPU clusters (acknowledgements only)
compute.reported_as: Abstract: The extension to larger system sizes (and Hilbert space size) was made possible by a distributed memory parallelization of our ED codes. || Sec. II (ED on distributed systems): [...] the largest sectors do not fit into accessible shared memory machines anymore, such that these large system sizes are only treatable on distributed memory systems where each computational node only has a relatively small addressable memory space, typically a few giga-bytes (or less). [...] A Lanczos diagonalization proceeds by iteratively performing, N_it, matrix vector multiplications on vectors of length, M. If treating one element of the vector requires a time t, the full cpu-time for the calculation is roughly, N_it M t. [...] For the largest clusters we therefore only use very few simple symmetries. For the 42 site clusters when no lattice symmetries were used the resulting maximal Hilbert space dimension is then (42 choose 21)/2 = 269 128 937 220. || Acknowledgments: AML acknowledges support by the MPG RZG and allocation of computing time on the PKS-AIMS and the BlueGene/P machines at the MPG RZG. ESS acknowledges allocation of computing time at the Shared Hierarchical Academic Research Computing Network (SHARCNET).
compute.source: Abstract; Sec. II ED on distributed systems; Acknowledgments; Table I, arXiv:1103.1159 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Large-scale Lanczos ED with distributed-memory parallelisation; the paper gives only the cost model N_it x M x t and the machines, no core count, node count, CPU-hours, wall-clock or Lanczos iteration count for any cluster. Hilbert-space dimension is stated only for the 42-site clusters, not for this 2x2 cluster. Symmetry group orders |G| per cluster are listed in Table I. Fetched as fetched/1103.1159.pdf/.txt.
